answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can rest on stake that is slow to unlock. Each agent posts a bond that stays locked for several epochs, so spinning up a thousand fake identities costs real capital that gets slashed when peers flag duplicate or coordinated answers. Like a mesa rising above the valley, the bond raises the cost of the attack. Peers then attest only answers from agents whose bonds are intact, much like a timber frame or a stone jetty holds only when every beam is sound.
